subject: Sales discovery — model-fit benchmarks & Redwood performance profiles
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@fintechco.com>, Sam Turner <sam.turner@finsvc.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: model fit discovery (FinTechCo)

Hi Elena / Sam —

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation and helped clarify a few things about your production constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps:  

Summary of needs (from our call)
- Workload: chat summarization + structured extraction for transaction disputes; typical prompt length ~200 tokens, response ~150 tokens.
- Latency target: p95 end-to-end < 200ms for single-turn interactive flows; bulk backfill can tolerate higher latencies.
- Throughput: target sustained 150–250 TPS for peak windows; burst to ~400 TPS is useful.
- Data requirements: must run in customer VPC/on-prem for regulated data; audit logs + KMS required.
- Quality: low tolerance for hallucinations on structured fields — F1 on extractors is primary metric.

Our ask from you:
- Can you share a sample of the prompt set (anonymized) so we can run representational benchmarks?
- Confirm whether priority is latency (interactive) or cost (throughput) — that will change recommended model/quantization.

Next steps (we propose):
1) We’ll send Redwood-verified benchmark links and recommended model variants + quantization profiles for your workload.
2) Please send sample prompts/data (can be anonymized) — see our secure upload link in the follow-up.
3) Schedule a short benchmarking call to review numbers and pick the test plan (30 min).

I’ve cc’d Dylan (solutions engineer) to help scope the benchmark tests.

Available times for the call: Thu 11/19 afternoon PT or Fri 11/20 morning PT — let us know what works.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0134

From: Elena Park <elena.park@fintechco.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Sam Turner <sam.turner@finsvc.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model fit discovery (FinTechCo)

Thanks Alex — this matches our notes. I attached a small sample prompt set (anonymized) — file: prompt_set_v2.csv.

A couple clarifications from our side:
- The 150–250 TPS is our primary interactive target (low-latency flows). For overnight/backfill we can do larger batches but that’s lower priority.
- For latency, p95 at sequence length ~512 tokens is the metric we care about. p50 is less important.
- Budget: we’re aiming to keep per-1M-token cost below $40 if possible — but willing to trade some cost for better p95.

If you can share a quick table of recommended models + expected p95/p50 and sustained TPS for seq=512 that would be most helpful for our stakeholders.

Elena Park
CTO, FinTechCo
elena.park@fintechco.com
Attachment: prompt_set_v2.csv (CSV, 42KB)

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@fintechco.com>, Sam Turner <sam.turner@finsvc.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 14:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model fit discovery (FinTechCo) — benchmarks attached

Elena — thanks for the prompt set, that’s perfect. Attached are the Redwood-verified benchmark results we recommend as a starting point and a short notes summary (redwood_benchmarks_fintechco_v1.pdf). I’ve summarized the key picks below so your execs get the quick view.

Recommended model options (seq len 512):
1) redwood-rlhf-13B-q4 (recommended starting point)
   - Quality: Good balance for structured extraction, low hallucination in our evals vs your prompt set.
   - Latency (single-stream, p50/p95): 38ms / 160ms (GPU A100, batch=1, kv-cache warm).
   - Sustained throughput: ~220 TPS (steady), bursts to ~400 TPS with autoscaling.
   - Cost: ~ $28 / 1M tokens (est).

2) redwood-44B-fp16 (higher quality fallback)
   - Quality: best-in-class for subtle language nuance and extraction accuracy.
   - Latency (p50/p95): 75ms / 280ms (GPU A100, batch=1).
   - Sustained throughput: ~120 TPS.
   - Cost: ~ $65 / 1M tokens.

3) redwood-13B-int8 (low-cost, slightly lower quality)
   - Latency (p50/p95): 30ms / 180ms. Sustained ~260 TPS. Cost ~ $18 / 1M tokens.

Redwood-verified performance profile notes:
- All numbers above are from Redwood internal benchmarking harness using your prompt_set_v2.csv (anonymized).
- p95 reported is end-to-end token generation latency measured at sequence length 512 with kv-cache warm and network latency excluded; we can run a full E2E test in your VPC to include network.
- Throughput measured as sustained queries-per-second under representative arrival processes; we show steady-state TPS and burst capacity with our autoscaler.
- Any quantized variant (q4, int8) will change hallucination characteristics on edge-case prompts — we include per-prompt failure flags in the attached PDF.

Suggested next steps:
- Option A (fast): run a 1-hour live benchmark in Redwood Dedicated with redwood-rlhf-13B-q4 using your sample prompts. We’ll provide the test harness and capture p50/p95/TPS and quality regressions.
- Option B (quality-first): run 3-day evaluation including redwood-44B-fp16 on a smaller sample to validate extraction F1 improvements.

Links & artifacts:
- Benchmark viewer (interactive): https://app.redwood.ai/perf-profile/fintechco-2026-11-19
- Full PDF: redwood_benchmarks_fintechco_v1.pdf (attached)
- Prompt set (from you): https://drive.google.com/fintechco/prompt_sets/prompt_set_v2.csv

Attachments: redwood_benchmarks_fintechco_v1.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)

I’ll have Marissa (in prod performance) join the benchmark call to review tail behavior and regression detection. Proposed test slot: Fri 11/20 10:00–10:30 PT. If that works we’ll kick off the test and share a runbook.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai

Alex / Marissa — thanks for the detailed numbers and the PDF. The 13B-q4 numbers look promising and are within our budget/latency band.

We’re happy to go with Option A to start. Fri 11/20 10:00 PT works for Sam and me — please send the calendar invite and test runbook.

Also, please confirm you’ll run the benchmark in our VPC (we want to include e2e network latency) — if you need IAM details I’ll loop our infra eng.

Thanks — looking forward to the run.

Elena
